summary.text: Kristin Roers is a Republican state senator from District 27 in Fargo who has served since December 2018 and is seeking re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election.
A nurse and nursing and clinical services consultant, she is the Senate majority caucus leader.

paragraphs.text: Kristin Roers was born in Lyon County, Minnesota, and raised in Sioux Falls, South Dakota, according to her Ballotpedia survey responses.
She holds a B.S. in economics and a B.S. in nursing from South Dakota State University and an M.S. in nursing and healthcare systems administration from the University of Minnesota.
She works as a nursing and clinical services consultant.
Roers assumed office on December 1, 2018, and advanced from the Republican primary on June 9, 2026.
Her legislative biography lists her as Senate majority caucus leader, chair of the State and Local Government Committee, and a member of the Human Services Committee.
In the survey, Roers listed property tax relief and reform, government efficiency, and strong communities as her key messages.
She named health care and human services, election law, and occupational licensing reform as policy areas she is passionate about.
She listed endorsements from the North Dakota Republican Party and District 27 Republicans, Governor Kelly Armstrong and Senator John Hoeven.
